messages:
maria: heads-up — canary run for quantized-raven-v2 produced ~0.8% func-call outputs that our json parser rejects. sample attached below.

aj: urgh, any pattern? truncated tail or extra junk? :thinking_face:

maria: mostly truncated closing braces or stray commas after arrays. here's one verbatim: ```{"action": "create_ticket", "params": {"title": "OOM on upload", "desc": "stacktrace..."``` (no closing `}}`)

kevin: that will trigger our retry loop and double-charge tokens. do we see it correlated with short responses or with max_new_tokens?

maria: tends to happen right around the 128-160 token mark. more frequent when kvcache prefix is non-empty.

raj: possible causes: kv cache truncation, EOS token mishandled during quantized decoding, or a detokenization bug in the runtime.

aj: can we add a lightweight post-parse validator in the client-side that attempts a quick fix (append `}` or wrap in array) before retrying? avoids extra model calls.

kevin: +1 for heuristic repair, but we need telemetry to avoid silent corruption. Capture: raw output, whether repair succeeded, repair kind, and downstream parse result. tag with model, quant config, seq_len, kvcache-size.

maria: ok I'll push a small change to the canary harness: 1) record raw token stream + bytes, 2) attempt two repairs (close braces, and try JSON5 tolerant parse), 3) only retry the model if repairs fail.

ci-bot: CI job queued — canary/quant-onboard/1759994444 will run with new validator.

raj: also add an EOS sentinel on the prompt that we strip server-side for scoring (e.g., `--END_OF_CALL--`). If the model emits it reliably we can cut off precisely and avoid partial json. Might reduce the failure class.

aj: agree, but verify it doesn't appear in user-visible payloads. strip and assert.

maria: will run the canary and post summary. if rates don't drop we escalate to runtime team for kernel/decoding investigation.

kevin: sweet. also add a quick dashboard metric: percent-repaired vs percent-retried vs total func_call events. helps decide whether to accept repair heuristics permanently. :thumbsup:
